interview.name: Pia
interview.answer: The timing and drop-off details still aren’t set, so the repair drive hasn’t been placed yet.

reflections: Pia is coordinating the timing and logistics before committing to details.
Faye is ready to help once the schedule is confirmed and wants early notice.
Nell is acting as a helpful intermediary by checking with others about timing and drop-off details.
Pia is the main coordinator and keeps asking for timing and drop-off details before making plans.
Faye, Cleo, and Ira are responsive helpers who defer to Pia and promise to update her once they have the needed details.
Nell is contributing indirectly by checking around for information, suggesting a group that is still in the information-gathering phase.
Pia is coordinating around shared timing and drop-off details and keeps others updated so they can plan accordingly.
Ira is actively gathering missing details stop by stop and communicates progress before promising a follow-up.
Eli and Oren are cooperative participants who wait for the needed details, with Oren adding a light reminder request and willingness to help.
Pia is the coordination hub, repeatedly waiting on details and relaying them to everyone else.
The group is aligned on a shared repair drive and is cooperating with low-friction follow-through.
Several people are eager to help, but they depend on Pia or others to confirm timing, logistics, and supplies first.
Pia is coordinating timing-sensitive details and is consistently transparent about waiting before sharing updates.
Cleo appears to be handling logistics on a parallel track, keeping supplies, venue access, and parking information moving.
The group is collaborating calmly and flexibly, with others offering to take on whatever help is needed once Pia’s details are ready.
